key_insight: A general-relativistic superfluid framework establishes necessary and sufficient conditions for nonlinear causality and strong hyperbolicity, enabling stable simulations of neutron-star vortex dynamics.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports computational studies of superfluid angular-momentum transport relevant to pulsar glitches and neutron-star dynamics.
method: Include entrainment, vortex forces, and vortex-line energy in relativistic two-fluid hydrodynamics.
Represent vortex dynamics using effective electric and magnetic fields and drift velocities.
Combine finite-volume evolution with constrained transport of superfluid vorticity and implicit electric-field updates.
evidence_signal: Validation includes an exact relativistic superfluid Riemann solution, Kelvin-wave dispersion relations, and oscillation modes of global two-fluid neutron-star equilibria.
watch_item: The simplified spin-down calculation prescribes vortex release and repinning, limiting conclusions about self-consistent glitch dynamics.
paper_title: Nonlinearly Causal General-Relativistic Superfluid Hydrodynamics: Simulating Vortex Dynamics in Neutron-Star Interiors
